enonce_markdown: Which salutation and ending are suitable for a letter to your close friend Neba?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

An informal letter is addressed to someone you know well. Use the first name in the salutation and a warm, friendly ending.

### Solution

For a close friend, the salutation uses the first name and the ending is warm: **c) Dear Neba ... Yours lovingly**.

- a) and b) are formal openings and endings used for officials.
- d) is too formal for a close friend.

choix.texte: Dear Sir ... Yours faithfully
To Whom It May Concern ... Yours obediently
Dear Neba ... Yours lovingly
Dear Mr Neba ... Yours respectfully

enonce_markdown: In an informal letter, where do you write your own address and the date?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Follow the standard layout: sender's address and date at the top (right), then the salutation, the body, the closing and the signature.

### Solution

The sender's address and the date go at the top right of the page: **a)**.

They are never placed at the bottom, in the centre or after the signature.

choix.texte: At the top right-hand corner
At the bottom left-hand corner
In the centre of the page
After your signature

enonce_markdown: The topic says: *"Your name is Ayuk Neba and your address is P.O. Box 45, Bali."* Which heading is correct for the letter?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Use exactly the name and address imposed by the topic, in the right place. Do not invent another address.

### Solution

The imposed address and the date are written at the top right: **b)**. The name Ayuk Neba is used as the signature at the end.

- a) leaves out the address and the date.
- c) uses the wrong address.
- d) puts the address in the wrong place.

choix.texte: Ayuk Neba only, at the top left
P.O. Box 45, Bali, and the date at the top right
The friend's address at the top right
P.O. Box 45, Bali, at the bottom of the letter

enonce_markdown: Which sentence has the right tone for a letter to a friend?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Informal letters use a warm, natural tone and simple language, as if you were speaking to the friend. Formal expressions are wrong here.

### Solution

Sentence **c)** is warm and natural, with a personal reaction.

Sentences a), b) and d) use formal expressions ("kindly be informed", "I wish to inform you", "humble request") which belong to formal letters.

choix.texte: Kindly be informed that I have passed my examination.
I wish to inform you that I have succeeded in my examination.
I am delighted to tell you that I have passed my exam. Imagine my joy!
It is my humble request that you congratulate me on my result.

enonce_markdown: You write an informal letter to a friend. Which opening sentence is the most suitable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

An informal letter opens with friendly greetings and good wishes, before the news. Business phrases belong to formal letters.

### Solution

A greeting and wish for good health, as in **c)**, is the natural opening of a letter to a friend.

The other options are formal or business openings.

choix.texte: I am writing to apply for the post of cashier.
With reference to your letter dated 3rd May,
I hope this letter finds you in good health and good spirits.
Please be informed that I have received your message.

enonce_markdown: You are Mbole Efua, P.O. Box 78, Kumba. Your friend Ndifor has moved to Douala. Write the layout (address, date and salutation) and the first paragraph only of a letter to Ndifor giving him the news that your school team has won the inter-school football cup. The paragraph must not exceed 80 words.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Informal letter: sender's address and date at the top right, a salutation with the first name, a friendly opening, then the news in a lively personal tone, within the word limit.

### Solution

**Model answer**

P.O. Box 78
Kumba
12th October 2026

Dear Ndifor,

I hope this letter finds you well and enjoying life in Douala. I have wonderful news! Last Saturday our school team beat Saint Paul's College 2-1 in the final and won the inter-school cup. I scored the winning goal in the last minute, and the whole crowd carried me on their shoulders. Everybody keeps asking when you will visit, because they say the team misses its best defender.

*(paragraph: 68 words)*

**Why this works.** The layout follows the imposed address and puts the date at the top right. The salutation uses the first name. The paragraph starts with good wishes, gives the news with personal detail (the winning goal), keeps a friendly tone with an exclamation, and links to the reader ("when you will visit"). It stays under 80 words.

**Common mistakes.** Forgetting the date, using a formal salutation or ending, or writing the whole letter instead of the layout and one paragraph.
